1_mint.note: The generic house masher (scripts/capture_start_state.py, undirected START/A pulses only) genuinely stalled forever on this ROM: tried at both --max-frames 2000 (default) and --max-frames 4000/--check-every 60, both returning 'never became controllable'. A rendered-frame probe (scratchpad, not committed) at f=1800 and f=3600 showed IDENTICAL frames -- MM3's stage-select screen, whose 3x3 grid's CENTER cell is a static Mega Man portrait / 'PUSH START' idle prompt, not a selectable robot-master box. This is exactly the directional-cursor-screen trap named in the task: an undirected masher can never leave it, and a RAM-only liveness heuristic run from that stuck point would never fire. Fixed with a custom scripted, frame-timed sequence: house masher through logo/story/title to f=1900 (stage-select fully up), then ONE RIGHT tap + START to move off the center decoration onto an adjacent box (landed on Top Man), then a 900-frame settle through the name-card + fade-in into live gameplay.
1_mint.cmd: custom script (scratchpad/mm3_mint.py, house masher f<1900 + RIGHT-tap + START + 900f settle) -- not scripts/capture_start_state.py, whose undirected masher cannot escape this screen
1_mint.liveness_probe: runs/onboard_wave5/mint_mega_man_3.json -- right_vs_left_120f=329, right_vs_noop_120f=337, left_vs_noop_120f=59, a_vs_noop_120f=30 (2KB RAM range)
1_mint.visual_confirmation: MANDATORY per task instructions -- rendered frame at the capture point shows live Top Man stage gameplay (conveyor-block room, Mega Man sprite, two HUD energy meters), not a menu/cursor/text screen. Also visually confirmed the FAILURE mode itself (identical stage-select frames at f=1800/f=3600) before attempting the scripted fix, ruling out 'just needs more time' the same way wave 4's Castlevania III / Power Blade mint_failed calls were confirmed with two independent probe designs.
1_mint.false_positive_note: This mint would have been vulnerable to exactly the RAM-only-heuristic trap the task warns about (a directional-cursor screen fooling input-divergence alone) IF the generic masher's stuck point had been probed with RIGHT-vs-LEFT-vs-NOOP directly -- moving the cursor left vs right from the stage-select screen DOES diverge RAM (different robot-master box highlighted), which could false-positive as 'live gameplay' on a cursor screen. Caught here by rendering the frame BEFORE trusting any RAM diff, per the task's explicit instruction.
